description: Voting Village at DEF CON 26 covers election security, voting machine vulnerabilities, and election infrastructure defenses. The talks explore election threats and solutions, voting machine forensics, auditing procedures, state and local election security perspectives, and trustworthy election systems.

talks.title: Defending Election Security A National Security Priority
talks.teaser: Election security as a national security priority: threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive strategies.
talks.summary:
### Election Security as National Security Infrastructure
At 00:00, Robert Karas, Director of National Cybersecurity Assessments and Technical Services (NCATS) at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), addresses the Voting Village on federal initiatives to protect election systems following the designation of election infrastructure as critical infrastructure.

### DHS Technical Assessment and Vulnerability Scanning Services
At 07:38, Karas details the free technical assessment services provided by DHS to state and local election officials. These offerings include automated external vulnerability scanning, comprehensive remote penetration testing, and on-site architecture reviews designed to identify security exposures before elections.

### Phishing Simulation Metrics and Training Campaigns
At 15:46, the presentation reviews empirical findings from simulated phishing engagements conducted with local election jurisdictions. Karas shares engagement statistics and highlights the necessity of training election staff to recognize deceptive spear-phishing attempts that could provide adversaries an initial foothold.

### Foundational Hygiene: MFA, Patching, and Access Control
At 23:28, Karas emphasizes that election defense depends on rigorous implementation of fundamental cybersecurity hygiene. He stresses the immediate adoption of multi-factor authentication, consistent operating system patching, and strict network segmentation across voter registration databases.

### Cross-Sector Collaboration and Trusted Intelligence Sharing
Concluding between 33:55 and 40:00, Karas discusses bridging the gap between federal intelligence agencies and local election administrators. He explains how DHS works to declassify actionable threat intelligence and establish trusted communication channels with state officials to defend the integrity of democratic elections.

talks.title: Mechanics and Pitfalls of Auditing with Scanners
talks.teaser: Challenges and methodologies for auditing voting systems using security scanning tools.
talks.summary:
### The Mechanics of Post-Election Scanner Audits
At 00:00, election security auditor Maggie MacAlpine delivers a technical lightning talk analyzing the hardware mechanics, image processing algorithms, and operational pitfalls of auditing paper ballots with commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) scanners.

### Re-Scanning 100% of Cast Ballots
At 02:05 and 04:00, MacAlpine explains the procedural imperative of post-election audits. Rather than trusting proprietary election-night tabulator software, independent audits verify election outcomes by rescanning all physical paper ballots using separate, high-speed commercial document scanners.

### The Threat of Automated Image Enhancement Drivers
At 06:00, the speaker highlights a critical technical pitfall: commercial scanner drivers are engineered to optimize document legibility. Automated features—including contrast enhancement, dynamic thresholding, edge smoothing, and background speckle reduction—modify the digitized image before saving.

### Distorting Voter Intent on Digital Ballots
At 08:01, MacAlpine demonstrates how automated scanner "helpfulness" compromises audit integrity. Contrast filters can unintentionally erase light pencil marks or fill in unvoted bubbles, introducing artificial discrepancies between the physical paper ballot and the digitized audit record.

### Enforcing Raw Image Capture for Legally Defensible Audits
Concluding the session, MacAlpine stresses that audit engineers must override and disable all automated image correction features. Preserving raw, uncompressed ballot scans ensures that audits reflect the true physical voter marks, providing legally defensible election verification.

talks.title: Trustworthy Elections
talks.teaser: Building trustworthy election systems through security principles and verification methods.
talks.summary:
### The Imperative for Mathematically Verifiable Elections
At 00:00, Dr. Joseph Kiniry, Chief Scientist at Galois and Free & Fair, presents on building provably trustworthy, verifiable voting systems at the Voting Village. Kiniry argues that public confidence in election outcomes requires mathematical proof rather than blind institutional trust.

### Dissecting Government and Vendor Reassurances
At 05:10, Kiniry evaluates public statements issued by government organizations such as NASS, NASED, DHS, and voting machine vendors. He contrasts claims that election systems are secure with empirical findings demonstrating widespread software flaws across commercial voting terminals.

### Moving From Blind Trust to Verifiable Systems
At 10:25, the speaker addresses the architectural dilemma of election security. While financial systems rely on identity tracking and transactional audit trails, voting systems must maintain absolute ballot secrecy while simultaneously providing universal verification that ballots were tallied accurately.

### End-to-End Verifiable (E2E-V) Cryptographic Voting
At 15:56, Kiniry details the design of End-to-End Verifiable (E2E-V) voting protocols. Under an E2E-V system, voters receive cryptographic proofs that allow them to independently verify that their ballot was recorded as intended and tallied as recorded, without revealing their candidate selection to anyone.

### Formal Verification and Open-Source Election Hardware
Concluding between 21:12 and 27:24, Kiniry showcases formally verified, open-source election hardware and software designs. He emphasizes that utilizing mathematically verified microkernels and open-source specifications ensures election infrastructure remains transparent, secure, and resilient against tampering.

talks.title: Return of Software Vulns in Brazilian Voting Machines
talks.teaser: Analysis of software vulnerabilities and security issues in Brazilian electronic voting machines.
talks.summary:
### Security Vulnerabilities in Brazilian Electronic Voting Machines
At 00:00, Professor Diego Aranha (Aarhus University) presents the findings of official public security testing evaluating the software and cryptographic architecture of Brazil's paperless Direct-Recording Electronic (DRE) voting machines.

### The Architecture of the Brazilian DRE Terminal
At 05:00, Aranha analyzes the Brazilian voting hardware. Deployed nationwide in fully paperless elections, each terminal loads its operating system, cryptographic keys, and ballot definition files from external flash memory cards prior to election day.

### Decades of Closed-Source Proprietary Code
At 10:02, the speaker critiques the institutional governance of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE). For decades, the voting software was developed behind closed doors without independent third-party code review, academic audits, or public verification.

### Physical Inspection Limits and Cryptographic Lapses
At 15:00 and 20:00, Aranha outlines severe cryptographic vulnerabilities discovered during inspection. Encryption keys protecting internal databases and firmware signatures were hardcoded directly into the C source code, shared identically across half a million voting machines nationwide, and seeded with weak pseudorandom number generators.

### Breaking the Secrecy of the Digital Ballot Box
Concluding at 25:00, Aranha details how his research team successfully broke ballot secrecy. By exploiting flaws in the software's vote-shuffling algorithm, researchers reconstructed the exact chronological order of cast ballots, proving that paperless DRE systems fail to guarantee constitutional ballot confidentiality.

talks.title: A Comprehensive Forensic Analysis of WINVote Voting
talks.teaser: Detailed forensic analysis of security vulnerabilities and design flaws in WINVote voting machines.
talks.summary:
### Forensic Post-Mortem of the AVS WINVote
At 00:00, Professor Carsten Schürmann presents an in-depth forensic investigation of the decommissioned AVS WINVote direct-recording electronic (DRE) touchscreen voting terminal at the Voting Village. Schürmann examines how flawed voting technologies persisted in American elections for over a decade.

### Deployment History and Decertification
At 04:45, Schürmann reviews the history of WINVote deployments. Manufactured in the early 2000s, these paperless touchscreen machines were used in municipal, state, and presidential elections across multiple jurisdictions until state authorities decertified the hardware in 2015 following catastrophic security failures.

### Digital Forensics with Autopsy
At 09:51, the presentation explores the forensic methodology used to examine extracted WINVote hard drives. Utilizing open-source forensic tools like Autopsy, Schürmann reconstructs partition tables, recovers deleted log files, and audits the system registry to evaluate the machine's operational history.

### Catastrophic Architectural Security Vulnerabilities
At 14:12, Schürmann reveals the compounding security flaws discovered in the hardware and software stack. The machines ran an unpatched Windows XP Embedded operating system, utilized default hardcoded database passwords (`admin1`), stored votes in cleartext Microsoft Access databases (`vote.mdb`), and maintained unsecured ad-hoc Wi-Fi interfaces that allowed remote administrative compromise from parking lots outside polling stations.

### The Role of Paper Trails and Risk-Limiting Audits
Concluding between 18:52 and 25:00, Schürmann emphasizes the vital importance of voter-verifiable paper audit trails (VVPAT) and post-election risk-limiting audits. He stresses that independent paper records are essential to verify election outcomes when electronic voting machines suffer hardware failures or malicious tampering.
